text:
Maria G.: Heads-up — BlueNova pushed back hard on the p99 SLO. They want ~150ms p95 and ~400ms p99 at their expected QPS. We can't hit both with the current kernel/packing behavior. Opening thread for triage + what we tell Sales/Product.

Dan: Which kernel rollout caused this? perf numbers?

Maria G.: The recent 2.3 kernel we promoted last Wed. Quick bench (BlueNova trace sample):
```
baseline kernel 1.9: p95=132ms, p99=280ms, avg=48ms
kernel 2.3: p95=148ms, p99=620ms, avg=55ms
KV miss-rate (2.3 run): 18% cold misses in first 30s
```
Tail exploded after a burst when KV warmed up. Microbatching heuristics also ended up coalescing too much for short queries.

Ryan: I dug into the profile. Two things stand out: (1) 2.3's fused attention kernel has slightly worse short-seq latency on this model shape, (2) our microbatch scheduler is batching 3-6 requests for sequences <64 tokens which increases single-request latency. KV cold-starts amplify 99th.

Alexa: Proposal for negotiation: run a two-tier offering for BlueNova:
- "low-latency" slice: kernel=1.9, microbatch max=2, reserved capacity (p95 target 150ms)
- "throughput" slice: kernel=2.3, microbatch max=8, best-effort p99 (with documented burst carveouts)
We can present engineering proof: p95 stable under low-latency config, p99 still high during cold-warm transitions.

Sales_Steve: BlueNova insists on both numbers for the same traffic until contract signature. Can we give them a canary period (2 weeks) with SLA opt-out if tail > target? Or offer a commercial credit window instead of hard p99?

Luci: Suggestion: quantify the expected window. From simulations, with prefix caching + prewarm, p99 drops to ~380-420ms after 45s of steady traffic. So we can propose:
- Guarantee p95=150ms for traffic on low-latency slice immediately.
- For global p99, guarantee 2x tier: 400ms after 60s steady-state; initial 60s carveout for cold starts and kernel switch regressions.
Include a surcharge for reserving prewarmed shards.

Dan: Ops ask: what changes to runtime if we offer low-latency slice? Kernel rollback on those pools + microbatch limit + aggressive KV prewarm. Need perf run numbers to sign off.

Maria G.: Actionable perf checklist I ran locally:
1) Run synthetic BlueNova replay on canary cluster (done, attached numbers).
2) KV warmup script: prefill top-10k prefixes, reduced cold miss-rate to 3%.
3) Microbatch sweep: sizes 1,2,4,8 — best p95 at 1-2 for short seqs, throughput wins at 4-8.
4) Kernel side-by-side: 1.9 better for p95 on short seqs; 2.3 better throughput for long seqs.

Ryan: I'll produce a 1-slide perf proof and git hash of bench. Also scheduling a short run to measure tail vs QPS with synthetic spikes.

Sales_Steve: If we go with tiered offering, I can propose: Low-latency tier (p95=150ms) at +20% price, Throughput tier at standard rate and explicit p99 carveouts. Will BlueNova accept a 60s warmup carveout clause?

Maria G.: Also note: we found a small regression in our KV path introduced by a race in 2.3 under high-concurrency that increases miss handling latency. Patch incoming. If we patch fast, we might be able to tighten the carveout window.

deploy-bot: deploy 1849994300 rolled back kernel 2.3 -> 1.9 in canary-cluster-7 :white_check_mark:

Alexa: Next steps before telling Sales:
- Ryan: bench + slide by EOD tomorrow
- Maria: run microbatch sweep with BlueNova traces, include KV miss histograms
- Ops: estimate cost for reserved prewarmed shards and add to proposal
- Sales_Steve: draft commercial language with 60s warmup carveout and credit terms

Maria G.: I'll update this thread with the bench link and final numbers. If we can get the KV fix merged today, the warmup carveout might be 30s instead of 60s.

Sales_Steve: Thanks — that buys me a path to keep the deal alive.

Luci: +1. Keep the messaging clear: we can meet p95 for low-latency fleet immediately; p99 requires either prewarm or an initial warmup window.

Maria G.: Filed follow-ups in GH: perf/bench-1849, kv/fix-1850, sales/proposal-1848. Back to work, will ping with numbers. :thumbsup:
